rfm_tuples.R: Management's Annual Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting ... our CEO and CFO concluded that our internal control over financial reporting was effective as of December 31, 2024. BUT Critical Audit Matter is on Revenue Recognition – Estimated contract costs and variable consideration estimates: 'high degree of subjectivity', and Note 2 discloses a $28.0M ($0.52 EPS) downward revision to 2024 net income from revisions in cost estimates on contracts in progress at 12/31/2023. rfm_tuples.R: We were in compliance with the covenants for the Credit Agreement at December 31, 2024. rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: Verify covenant compliance and liquidity. Q1 2025 reversed: contract liabilities -$62M, contract assets +$165M.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: No covenant or liquidity stress. Capital structure de-risked aggressively in 2024 and Q1 2025. The mix of operating cash (customer advances vs. earned receivables) is worth flagging but is normal volatility for a percentage-of-completion contractor and does not rise to a red flag.

rfm_tuples.R: Although we have not been dependent upon any one customer in any year, a small number of customers tend to constitute a substantial portion of our total revenue in any given year. The 10-K paints concentration as stable/declining; the 10-Q (filed 9 weeks later) shows it climbing. Quiet drift, not lying, but the 10-K narrative is selective.

rfm_tuples.R: During the year ended December 31, 2024, certain contracts had revisions in cost estimates from those projected at December 31, 2023. This change in estimate resulted in a decrease in net income of $28.0 million, or $0.52 basic earnings per share and $0.51 diluted earnings per share for the year ended December 31, 2024.

FY24 MD&A also attributes Utilities GP recovery to 'productivity issues on some legacy projects from our PLH acquisition experienced in 2023 and higher costs associated with a communications project in 2023' — i.e., 2023 results were ALSO depressed by PLH-project re-estimates. Q1 2025 10-Q discloses an ADDITIONAL $5.2M Q1 revenue hit from 'changes in estimates associated with performance obligations satisfied prior to December 31, 2024.' Plus FY24 forward-looking statements list 'results of the review of prior period accounting on certain projects' as a forward risk.

Q1 2025 already discloses a fresh $5.2M hit on top. This is the textbook 'percentage-of-completion catch-up' pattern that historically precedes larger writedowns at E&C contractors. The 10-K language minimizes it as a one-off 'revision'; the recurring pattern says otherwise.

rfm_tuples.R: We had bid and payment/performance bonds issued and outstanding totaling approximately $8.1 billion. rfm_tuples.M_value: Bond face value JUMPED $2.2B (+37%) YoY ($5.9B -> $8.1B) while remaining performance obligation on bonded projects only rose $0.3B ($2.7B -> $3.0B). Implied unused bonded capacity grew ~$1.9B in one year.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Bond capacity expansion of 37% YoY indicates sureties remain comfortable underwriting PRIM despite the contract-cost catch-up issues. This is a real positive Mode B signal — a sophisticated counterparty (the surety market) is voting in favor of the company's solvency.

The FY24 10-K filed February 24, 2025 contained no indication of management instability; 25 days later the CEO who signed it was gone. summary: PRIM is a well-capitalized SP600 E&C contractor with a 19-year auditor relationship, unqualified ICFR opinion, full revolver availability, and 37% YoY surety-bond capacity growth — the macro signals say solvent, not distressed. But three Mode B signals are hard to reconcile with the 10-K's confident tone: (1) a $28.0M adverse prior-period contract-cost re-estimate in FY24 (~15% of net income) tied to legacy PLH backlog, followed by another $5.2M hit in Q1 2025, with a recurring pattern dating back to FY23; (2) the FY24 10-K's forward-looking-statements section quietly added 'review of prior period accounting on certain projects' and 'governmental investigations and/or inquiries' as new risk categories while Item 9 disclosed 'None' for accountant disagreements and Note 12 disclosed no material litigation — asymmetric reservation language; (3) the CEO sold $5.15M of stock on March 17, 2025 and was separated without cause 3 days later (March 20) with $1.95M cash severance, less than a month after signing the 10-K. Energy segment backlog also dropped ~10% QoQ in Q1 2025. Verdict: not a fraud case, but the recurring percentage-of-completion catch-ups and the CEO-departure / insider-sale timing fit the framework's profile of a name where the 10-K materially understates emerging operational and governance stress.
